newsitem.title: FRANCE: France confirms Dassault, Aerospatiale to merge.
newsitem.headline: France confirms Dassault, Aerospatiale to merge.

text.p: The French government Tuesday confirmed that state-owned Aerospatiale and combat plane maker Dassault Aviation would merge into a single company, with a single supervisory board and executive committee.

President Jacques Chirac announced a plan to create a single French aircraft manufacturer out of Aerospatiale and Dassault last February as part of a restructuring of the defence industry around a few national champions.

"The linkup will be through a merger of the two companies," the finance ministry said in a statement. "The management of the new group will be constituted through a single supervisory board and an executive committee."
The government will ask the independent Privatisation Commission to decide on the current valuations of the two firms and give its opinion on the merger terms, the statement said.
Dassault declined to comment on the statement. Aerospatiale officials were not immediately available.

The new group will pool a large part of the companies' research and purchasing activities, as well as creating centralized departments to oversee finance, industrial strategy, international relations, quality, human resources, communications and legal affairs, it said.

The group's industrial operations will be centred on divisions or subsidiaries handling combat planes and business jets, passenger aircraft, space and defence, helicopters and maintenance, the statement said.
Once the Privatisation Commission has given its views, the government will formally approve the transaction terms, which will be carried out with the approval of stock market authorities, it said.

The merged company will have annual revenues of about 60 billion francs ($11.36 billion) and will give Aerospatiale a significant military activity to complement its missiles and helicopter interests.

Industry analysts have said it was important for Aerospatiale to have Dassault within the group as it gives Aerospatiale greater weight in key negotiations over the planned change in status of the Airbus Industrie consortium.
Aerospatiale is a member of the Airbus grouping, along with British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
The Airbus partners want to change its partnership structure to a joint-stock company but are divided over the shape of the future company.
